answer: One robust defence is collateralised vouching. A new agent cannot mint an identity: it must be vouched for by established peers who lock a separate, non-transferable stake behind that endorsement, like a marble marker on a single square. If the newcomer is later exposed as a duplicate, the vouchers' stakes are slashed, so each fake costs its sponsors real, unshareable loss. A lone signal of honesty is cheap to fake, but a saffron-threaded web of distinct endorsements is not: an attacker must bribe a fresh set of sponsors for every extra identity, so cost grows linearly with the Sybil army.
